correctness.rationale: Every integral monic divisor of \(X^n-1\) corresponds to a subset of distinct cyclotomic factors. The product identity \(H_A(z)\prod_j H_A(z^{(p-1)p^{j-1}})\) is derived exactly. Since \(A<p-1\) and \(A<p\), reduction modulo p-1 isolates the first digit, and base-p expansion isolates all remaining digits. Coefficient products yield the exact \(2^r\) histogram. Allowed degrees form blocks indexed by restricted base-p words; their successor carries give precisely the stated gap lengths and counts. The normalized sets converge in Hausdorff distance <=\(p^{-b}\) to a separated affine IFS, giving dimension \(\log(A+1)/\log p\). Direct independent integer convolution verifies 96 triples, 510728 coefficients and 34336 gaps; this finite computation is corroborative, not the infinite proof. The uniform subset-product measure makes the layer digits independent with weights \(1/(2A)\) at the endpoints and \(1/A\) at interior digits; a bounded-coupling argument proves weak convergence. Strong cylinder separation and the law of large numbers give the exact-dimensional entropy formula \((\log A+(\log2)/A)/\log p\).

value.rationale: The complete distribution of monic divisor degrees, their precise fiber sizes, the contiguous missing-degree intervals with exact length census, and a natural limiting Hausdorff dimension are intrinsic invariants of \(X^{2^a p^b}-1\). They provide sharp complement-side information across infinitely many polynomial indices, contrasting the known all-degree/no-unique-interior-degree regime. It is a motivated complete classification of previously undetermined quantities, not a mere failure-of-practicality observation or an isolated numerical slice. The proof is elementary and no broader generalization is claimed. The distinct support dimension and typical divisor-degree dimension, \(\log(A+1)/\log p\) versus \((\log A+(\log2)/A)/\log p\), quantify an intrinsic sparse-multiplicity bias not visible from a bare coverage criterion.
